comments.body: By analyzing the blame information on this pull request, we identified @Morhaus, @vvo and @bobylito to be potential reviewers

New version shipped. 
Let me know what you think. Especially also on the mergeClassNames part. Until we add full inline style support, providing your own class (either with css-module or using a plain css file) will be the only way to extend a theme (otherwise, you need to redefine it completely).

@vvo Long comment here :) 

Well, I understand your point. It's true that if you don't want to follow a tutorial or you already done it, there's no references to go look after. 

However, when discussing with @bobylito, I really like the idea to have a tutorial for styling that will follow the one of the getting started. It may not be for everyone, but It can be a way to show how you can style our widgets (there's a lot of ways to do it...) based on a simple example. Of course, for now without inline style to perform small customizations, I believe it's not that powerful. But it's definitely a feature that I think we need to add. 

In the end, maybe we can have both: a quick tutorial and a reference guide? 
Do you think it will perform the same kind of jobs twice and this will be useless in the end?
Closing while you rework it/rework the styling API. Let's get this right right now

title: docs(styling): add tutorial about styling + renaiming
